purpose: Records the two track-conditional runtime floors gate3_runtime.py enforces, and the derivation/source of each Track B number, per this housekeeping task's ACCEPTANCE requirement ('GATE3.json carries two floors with the Track B floor's derivation source'). This gate exists to catch a stub/no-op phase silently standing in for real per-sample work -- see gates/gate3_runtime.py.
why_two_floors: A single floor cannot bind on both a toy/SIMULATED run (legitimately fast) and a Track B run claiming real exome-scale work (which must take materially longer). The previous single-floor design passed a synthetic run but would never bind on the one case that actually matters: a Track B run claiming exome-scale work it did not do.

TRACK_S.description: Floors for SIMULATED/toy-scale runs (this repo's actual current state -- TRACK.md: Track A only, no germline access, so every run so far has been Track S). Deliberately small.
TRACK_S.source_note: Unchanged from this gate's original design (see the prior task's DEPLOYMENT_LOG.md entries) -- calibrated only to catch a stub finishing in milliseconds on toy inputs, not to model real-world runtime. Not literature-derived; there is no publishable 'toy-scale runtime' to cite.

TRACK_B.description: Floors for a Track B run claiming real, exome-scale tool execution. Derived from real, live-cited tool runtimes wherever a genuine citation could be found; explicitly left UNVERIFIED (null) where none could be found, per Standing Rule 3 ('otherwise write UNVERIFIED and stop') -- never filled in with an invented number.

citations_found.claim: "~30 minutes with 12 CPUs from BAMs to CNA profiles" (fast purity/ploidy fit)
citations_found.scale: WGS (explicitly under the README's WGS subsection; no WES-specific figure exists in this source)
citations_found.used_as: base figure for this floor (1800 sec)

citations_found.claim: snp-pileup step: 2 CPUs, 4 GB, 1.5 hour; FACETS R analysis step: 2 CPUs, 40 GB, 15 minutes -- for one WGS tumor/normal CRAM pair (30-40x)
citations_found.note: corroborating figure (6300 sec total), not used as the base -- see derivation note
citations_found.caveat: a third-party teaching document, not FACETS' own official documentation (which contains no runtime statement at all)

citations_checked_but_not_usable.reason: the only figure found (~40 minutes) is explicitly for a heavily subsetted toy dataset (first 60Mb of chr5 only, ~1.9% of the genome) in a teaching tutorial, not a real-scale exome/genome run -- too weak to cite as a real-world figure

track_b_derivation.derivation_note: No WES-specific runtime citation exists for any of these three tools despite a genuine search (see GATE_HOUSEKEEPING.md) -- only WGS figures. Floor = smaller of the two WGS citations (ASCAT, 1800 sec) divided by an explicitly ARBITRARY, disclosed 20x conservatism factor (not itself literature-derived) intended to keep the floor safely permissive for WES's much smaller target footprint while remaining far above what a stub/no-op could produce (milliseconds). This is a weaker citation chain than this repo's BENCHMARKS_ROW-sourced numbers (PARAMETER_PROVENANCE.tsv convention) and is flagged as such rather than presented as literature-precise.

citations_found.claim: "Determine the scar scores with scarHRD R package. This step only takes a few minutes" (README contrasts this with copy-number calling, which it calls "time-consuming and compute-intensive"); operates on WES or WGS segmentation output
citations_found.scale: stated as applicable to WES or WGS segmentation input; no separate WES-vs-WGS runtime distinction given
citations_found.caveat: qualitative only -- no numeric minutes/hours figure exists anywhere in the source; repo's last commits are from 2020, so this documentation is several years old

track_b_derivation.derivation_note: No numeric figure exists in the source. 'A few minutes' is interpreted at its conservative low end (2 minutes = 120 sec) -- an explicitly ARBITRARY interpretation of a qualitative phrase, disclosed rather than presented as a precise citation. Floor = 120 sec / an ARBITRARY 5x conservatism margin (smaller than copy_number_calling's 20x because scarHRD runs on already-computed segmentation output, a much smaller data structure not expected to scale with WES-vs-WGS the same way copy-number calling does; the margin here mainly compensates for the qualitative/stale source, not a track-scale difference).

citations_checked_but_not_usable.reason: official GitHub repo (AlexandrovLab/SigProfilerAssignment) README contains no runtime/performance statement. A WebSearch snippet suggested a COSMIC assignment-tool page states low-mutation-count samples take 'about 15 seconds', but this could not be confirmed by direct fetch (cancer.sanger.ac.uk is blocked by this session's network egress policy) and is therefore NOT reported as verified, per Standing Rule 3. The primary paper (Diaz-Gay et al., Bioinformatics 2023, btad756) reportedly contains a CPU-time/memory benchmarking table per search snippets, but academic.oup.com/biorxiv.org/pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov are all blocked by this session's egress proxy, so the actual numbers could not be read or verified.

track_b_derivation.derivation_note: Per Standing Rule 3 ('otherwise write UNVERIFIED and stop'), no numeric Track B floor is asserted for this phase. gate3_runtime.py treats this as a hard failure (BLOCKED) whenever a Track B phase log includes a signature_assignment entry -- this phase's runtime tripwire cannot be validated until a real citation is found (e.g. from a network environment that can reach academic.oup.com / cancer.sanger.ac.uk). This gap is reported prominently (Standing Rule 8), not silently worked around by reusing the Track S floor or inventing a number.

This project's own in-house stdlib binomial-test code (PROTOCOL.md §5.2), not a third-party tool with a published runtime to cite. Its per-variant cost (an exact binomial p-value computation) is inherently lightweight and not expected to differ meaningfully between a toy-scale and a real exome-scale run, so the same floor is used for both tracks -- a disclosed design choice, not an oversight.

This project's own in-house MAF second-hit scan code (PROTOCOL.md §5.5), not a third-party tool with a published runtime to cite. Same rationale as loh_binomial_test: lightweight, per-variant, not expected to meaningfully change between tracks.

network_egress_caveat: This session's network egress proxy blocks essentially all non-GitHub domains (academic.oup.com, cran.r-project.org, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, biorxiv.org, cancer.sanger.ac.uk, etc.) -- confirmed repeatedly. Only GitHub-hosted pages (official repo READMEs, and third-party GitHub-hosted teaching material) could be fetched directly. The primary papers most likely to carry real per-exome benchmarking tables (FACETS, Sequenza, scarHRD, SigProfilerAssignment) could not be read from this environment. If a future session has broader network access, re-attempting this research against those primary sources -- especially the SigProfilerAssignment paper (Diaz-Gay et al. 2023, Bioinformatics btad756) -- is the clear next step to replace the UNVERIFIED signature_assignment floor and tighten the ARBITRARY conservatism margins above with real WES-specific figures.
